title: How a spell-checker counts the edits between two words
mechanism: Each cell takes the smallest of the three cells before it, and adds one when its two letters differ.
claim: The last cell holds the fewest edits that turn one word into the other, and no cell is worked out twice.
implication: Two words of ten letters cost a hundred cells, not the millions of ways to edit one into the other.

beats.title: The edges
beats.plain: The top row and the first column are plain counting: that many letters added, or taken away.

beats.title: One cell
beats.plain: A cell looks at the three before it, takes the smallest, and adds one because F is not L.

beats.title: Row by row
beats.plain: Every other cell is filled the same way, each from cells that are already there.

beats.title: The corner
beats.plain: The last cell is the answer: two edits turn flaw into lawn.
